title: review-signature/v1
description: targets/<id>/review/signatures/<role>-<date>-<n>.yaml (F26-R1, R9; D-9 v3.39): one signer's decision, by role — the intent signer that the surviving cluster says what the conjecture says, the independent signer that the evidence supports it — as accept, split (the clusters are genuinely different readings, D-30 v3.39) or send-back with a question. A signature is a decision written by a person; the page never computes one. Signed through the site by the approval key naming the login, or by the signer's own key. Versioned, never edited (D-34).

target.description: the target the record is filed under

cluster.description: the candidate representing the cluster accepted or chosen as the root; null for a send-back

question.description: the question a send-back raises; null otherwise

login.description: the GitHub login the record names, as a v3.33 approval does

via.description: how the signature was made (D-3, D-32 v3.33): `approval-key` through the service for a login signed in on the site; `ssh` by the signer's own key

key.description: the SSH public key the signature verifies under: the network's approval key (`via: approval-key`, equal to keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree) or the signer's own

signature.description: an OpenSSH SSHSIG armored signature over the record's canonical body (opn_gate.signed), made with the private half of `key`

id.description: the record's id, lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens; a candidate's is `c-<8 hex>` of its Lean's sha256, a test's `t-<8 hex>`, a question's `q-<n>`, an exhibit's `e-<8 hex>`
